findings.title: Committed prompt/audit corpus bloats the repo and review surface
evidence: git ls-files prompts | wc -l = 632 files; git ls-files -z prompts | xargs -0 du -cb = 9,421,195 bytes (~9.0 MiB) across 6 vendored packs (hardening 70, webstore 193, 60-modules 222, portal-alignment 63, repo-deep-dive 53, repo_audit 28)

prompts/PROVENANCE.md — 630 files pinned in prompts/manifest.json (SHA-256 per file + per-pack tree hashes); the 2026-10-03 note records that the five dated prior-run snapshots (157 files) were removed (INV-P3-001)
scripts/verify-prompts.js — verify mode recomputed by hand (Python replica of the utf8+CRLF-normalised SHA-256): 630/630 hashes match, 0 mismatches at 8d299b8d; CI runs it in validate.yml
git ls-files docs/audits = 75 files / 2,729,701 bytes; docs/audits/README.md defines the run-directory output contract
7 tracked *.pyc files under prompts/**/__pycache__/ and binary xlsx/docx/png assets are inside the pinned corpus
findings.impact: ~12 MiB of historical prompt/audit material is cloned, indexed and reviewed on every change; it dominates the diff surface for a repo whose application code is ~6 MB per app. The pinning guard prevents silent tampering but also freezes generated binaries (.pyc, xlsx) as 'content'.
findings.recommendation: Owner decision: keep the pinned corpus but move it to a separate read-only repo or a release artifact, and drop the two remaining generated binaries from the pin; at minimum add a note to CONTRIBUTING.md that prompts/ is historical data, not product code.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: prior-run snapshots are gone and the manifest verifies clean (630/630); the 632-file / 9.4 MB corpus remains committed. Same status as the 20261004 register (previously partially-fixed, owner decision).

findings.title: Duplicate product catalogs have diverged
evidence: apps/api/src/data/products.json (3,522,201 B) vs apps/web/lib/catalog/data/products.json (2,533,263 B): 245 common SKUs, all 245 differ in the same 6 fields (marketingCopy, customerOutcomes, whatIsIncluded, bestFor, internalProcedure, fulfillmentWorkflow) — Python structural diff at 8d299b8d

git log apps/web/lib/catalog/data/products.json — 2918891e/cce023c9 'Enrich store catalog: hand-authored ... copy for all 245 products'; the API copy was never re-synced (last touched 62de9c1b/81b54a85)

prompts/mct-full-webstore-product-catalog-pack/data/products.json and .../repo_patch/apps/web/lib/catalog/products.json are a third byte-identical copy (md5 d1efd7fe...), differing from both app copies
apps/api/src/lib/store-catalog.ts:1 imports the API copy as the fallback catalog; scripts/seed-store.ts:4 reads apps/api/src/data/products.json
AGENTS.md:94-95 records the divergence as known debt ('Reconcile to one canonical catalog ... when the catalog content workflow is defined')
no guard: grep products.json in .github/ and both app test trees returns no sync/equality check
findings.impact: The API/seed path serves the short reverted copy while the web storefront serves the enriched copy, so the same product reads differently depending on the surface; every content edit must be made twice, and the third copy inside the prompt pack will drift silently.
findings.recommendation: Pick one canonical source (suggest apps/web copy + a build/seed step), delete the API duplicate and the prompt-pack data copies, and add a CI check that any remaining copy is byte-identical or generated from the canonical file.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: still 245/245 products divergent in 6 content fields; AGENTS.md now documents it as open known debt but no code or guard changed. Previously partially-fixed at 9c0b88c; residual unchanged.

findings.title: Stale and machine-specific generated documentation
evidence: Fixed instance: AGENTS.md:3 and review.md:9 now say `MaineCyberTech/mainecybertech` (commit 3e53b3da 'chore: close HYG-P3-001'); review.md is guarded by scripts/sync-review-md.mjs --check in .github/actions/unit-tests/action.yml:63
docs/GAP_ANALYSIS.md:149 — 'comparative audit against reference repo `C:\temp\chat`'
docs/MT-P0-001-RLS-remediation-design.md:5 — 'Repo: `C:\temp\mainecybertech-portal` (branch `develop`)'

docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/REAUDIT_REPORT_20261004.md:9-10,20-26,208 — `C:\temp\reaudit\<repo>\VERIFY.md` and `file:///C:/temp/...` links to files that exist only on the author's machine (added 2026-10-04, after the HYG-P3-001 fix)
no tracked text has CRLF issues (git ls-files --eol: 0 crlf files) — this is a path-content problem, not an EOL problem
findings.impact: Operators and future agents reading these tracked docs see absolute Windows paths that resolve nowhere; the AGENTS.md instance was the one that misled agents about the repo location, and the class has already reappeared in the audit report published a day later.
findings.recommendation: Replace machine paths with repo-relative or URL references in the three files; extend scripts/check-docs-links.mjs (or a small grep gate) to fail on `C:\` / `file:///C:` in tracked markdown.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: the AGENTS.md/review.md fix is present and effective, but 3 other tracked docs still carry machine-specific paths (one of them published after the fix). Downgraded from verified-fixed to partially-fixed.

findings.title: Generated artifacts are inconsistently tracked
evidence: .gitignore:58-65 ignores sbom.cdx.json, sbom.spdx.json and licenses.json; git ls-files for those names returns nothing (exit 1)
.github/actions/dependency-audit/action.yml:31-40 — 'Ensure generated license/SBOM artifacts stay untracked' fails the job when git ls-files finds licenses.json / sbom.cdx.json / sbom.spdx.json
the guard action is wired into .github/workflows/test.yml:52 (PR) and .github/workflows/validate.yml:17 (deploy gate)
commit 3e7a39bb removed the committed licenses.json and added the gate (HYG-P3-002 / INV-P2-001)
findings.impact: The specific artifacts that previously drifted (license aggregate, SBOM) can no longer be committed, so a stale copy cannot masquerade as current. Residual instances of tracked generated files are filed separately (see 'Committed Python bytecode and a stale build artifact are tracked').
findings.recommendation: None for this scope; keep the guard. Apply the same ignore-and-gate pattern to apps/web/public/version.json and __pycache__ (separate finding).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: guard present and wired into both CI paths; licenses.json/sbom.* untracked. Previous status verified-fixed holds.

findings.title: 17 tracked shell scripts lack the exec bit; documented ./scripts/... commands fail
evidence: git ls-files -s '*.sh' at 8d299b8d: 19 files, all mode 100755, 0 at 100644
.github/workflows/validate.yml:19-31 — 'Verify tracked shell scripts are executable' (PORT-001) fails the deploy gate if any tracked *.sh is 100644
docs/ROLLBACK_PROCEDURES.md:141,175 and README.md:93-95 still document ./scripts/... invocation, which now works on Linux/macOS
findings.impact: Closed: operators following the incident/rollback docs no longer hit 'Permission denied', and the guard prevents reintroduction.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: 19/19 tracked .sh are 100755 and validate.yml:19-31 fails closed on any 100644. Previously verified-fixed at 9c0b88c (PR #74).

findings.title: AdminDocumentsCenterClient.tsx is a 2,322-line single component
evidence: apps/web/components/admin/AdminDocumentsCenterClient.tsx — 2,322 lines; one default-exported component (line 271) plus ~30 file-local helpers (docName/docDescription/FileThumb/ConfirmModal/... at lines 63-270)
26 useState/useEffect occurrences in the same file (grep -c)

next largest non-generated source files: apps/web/lib/module-actions.ts 1,690; apps/worker/src/tasks/module-tasks.ts 1,639; apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts 1,261; apps/web/components/admin/ProjectTaskListV5.tsx 1,013
coverage for the file exists (apps/web __tests__ route coverage 271 suites) so a split can be verified incrementally
findings.impact: The admin documents center concentrates document CRUD, visibility, preview, upload and org branding state in one module; every change risks unrelated regressions and review is effectively impossible line-by-line.
findings.recommendation: Extract the row/thumbnail/confirm-modal helpers and the upload/preview state machines into sibling files (AdminDocumentsTable, DocumentUploadDialog, useDocumentFilters); target <600 lines per file.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; no previous register row covers component size.

findings.title: Dead modules and a dead component with zero references
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/feature-flags.ts:8,17 — isFeatureEnabled/getFeatureFlags; `git grep -n 'isFeatureEnabled|getFeatureFlags'` across all tracked files returns 0 hits outside the file

apps/web/lib/catalog/proposal-actions.ts:2 — generateProposal server action (returns a hardcoded URL); 0 hits for the exact symbol outside the file (generateProposalDraft* matches are a different feature)
apps/web/lib/subnav-styles.ts:1 — navClass; 0 references repo-wide
apps/web/components/store/CategoryVisualHeader.tsx:34 — default export; 0 imports; only the prompt pack mentions the name
all four files were last touched between 2026-07-25 and 2026-07-29 and never referenced since
findings.impact: Dead modules imply functionality that does not exist (a feature-flag system, a proposal generator, a nav-style helper, a category header) and inflate the review surface; the proposal action is a stub that returns ok:true without doing anything.
findings.recommendation: Delete the three modules and the component in one cleanup PR; if any is planned work, move it to a tracked issue instead of shipping a stub.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Only CategoryVisualHeader.tsx surfaced from a whole-tree orphan scan; the three lib modules were confirmed by exact-symbol grep.

findings.title: Orphaned one-off catalog scripts and their 1.2 MB content-map pipeline
evidence: 7 scripts have zero references in .github/, package.json, apps/ or packages/: apply-content-map.js, fix-apostrophe.js, fix-cat.js, fix-everything-dupes.js, generate-details.js, generate-fulfillment.js, generate-product-content.js

scripts/apply-content-map.js:5-6 reads scripts/content-map/ and scripts/content-map-fulfillment/ (24 JSON files, 1.2 MB) and is itself unreferenced; all 490 map entries already match product ids baked into apps/web/lib/catalog/data/products.json
scripts/generate-details.js:263-264 destructively rewrites the 2.5 MB catalog: fs.unlinkSync(products.json) then renameSync(products-temp.json)
none of the seven appear in scripts/README.md (see the stale-index finding); seed-store.ts (also 0 CI references) is at least mentioned in docs
findings.impact: Re-running an undocumented one-off generator can overwrite the hand-enriched catalog (the exact copy that already diverged from the API copy); the pipeline's existence implies a content workflow that no longer exists.
findings.recommendation: Move the seven scripts plus both content-map directories to an archive branch/tag, or delete them; if they are kept, list them in scripts/README.md under a clearly marked 'one-off / do not run' heading.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Overlaps the catalog-divergence finding but is independently actionable (file cleanup).

findings.title: Committed Python bytecode and a stale build artifact are tracked
evidence: git ls-files | grep -E '__pycache__|\.pyc$' = 7 files, e.g. prompts/hardening_prompt_pack/engine/global_risk/__pycache__/global_risk_engine.cpython-314.pyc and prompts/portal-alignment/engine/{analytics,diff,remediation,trends}/__pycache__/*.pyc; .gitignore has no __pycache__/.pyc entry
the .pyc files are pinned in prompts/manifest.json, so the integrity guard freezes compiled bytecode as reviewed content

apps/web/public/version.json is tracked and stale: {branch:'unknown', run:'0', sha:'unknown', date:'2026-08-05T00:46:23.829Z'}; apps/web/scripts/generate-version.js rewrites it on every build (apps/web/package.json 'build': 'pnpm generate:version && next build') and .gitignore does not list it
findings.impact: Compiled bytecode from a developer's Python 3.14 environment is committed (clutter, potential leak of local paths/symbols); the tracked version.json serves 'unknown/0' version data whenever a build step is skipped, and its committed copy contradicts the current commit.
findings.recommendation: git rm the seven .pyc files, add __pycache__/ and *.pyc to .gitignore, regenerate prompts/manifest.json, and either untrack apps/web/public/version.json or generate it in CI before deploy.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; distinct from HYG-P3-002 (licenses/SBOM gate) which remains verified-fixed.

findings.title: Stray duplicate snippet file with local dev auth seed data
evidence: supabase/snippets/Untitled query 314.sql (filename contains spaces) is byte-identical to supabase/seeds/00_local_auth_users.corrected.v2.sql — both md5 493f2c58224ffd1119b965b415d2bbac
the file contains 2 INSERT blocks with auth.users rows including encrypted_password hashes for the local demo users (values redacted); it was added in the initial commit 4a87279f and never touched
git grep for 'supabase/snippets' or 'Untitled query' outside prompts/docs returns no consumer; the whole supabase/snippets/ directory is otherwise empty
findings.impact: A misleading duplicate of a seed file sits where a Supabase Studio 'save snippet' artifact would land; it invites edits to the wrong copy and keeps dev credential hashes in a second location. Low live risk (local-only users, bcrypt hashes).
findings.recommendation: Delete supabase/snippets/Untitled query 314.sql (keep the seeds/ copy) or move it under supabase/seeds/ with a clear name if it is intentionally kept.

findings.title: Root package script `sbom:licenses` is known-broken on the pinned pnpm
evidence: package.json:27 — "sbom:licenses": "pnpm licenses list --json > licenses.json" with "packageManager": "pnpm@10.34.3"

.github/actions/dependency-audit/action.yml:22-24 — comment: 'Uses scripts/collect-licenses.mjs, NOT `pnpm licenses list --json`, which exits 1 on pnpm 10.34.x and writes an error document to stdout (ERR_PNPM_MISSING_PACKAGE_INDEX_FILE)'

scripts/collect-licenses.mjs:5-13 — reproduces the failure ('on pnpm v10.34.3 after any install, exits 1 and writes {"error":{...}} to STDOUT ... the shell redirect produced a licenses.json containing an error object')
.github/workflows/sbom.yml:36-43 — the workflow was switched to scripts/collect-licenses.mjs for the same reason
findings.impact: A developer following the root script silently writes an error document to licenses.json, then gets a confusing failure from license-gate/SBOM; three code comments document the breakage but the script was never updated.
findings.recommendation: Change the script to "node scripts/collect-licenses.mjs --out licenses.json" (matching CI) and delete the `pnpm licenses list` invocation.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; CI itself is unaffected (it already uses the working script).

findings.title: scripts/README.md index is stale: 14 scripts (10 active CI guards) are undocumented
evidence: scripts/README.md:3 — 'Last updated 2026-08-01'

14 scripts present on disk but absent from the README index: apply-content-map.js, backfill-profile-pii.mjs, check-docs-counts.mjs, check-docs-links.mjs, check-required-checks.mjs, check-rls-predicate.mjs, collect-licenses.mjs, generate-db-types.js, generate-details.js, openapi-audit.js, seed-store.ts, sync-review-md.mjs, verify-prompts.js, verify-rls.mjs
10 of those are executed by CI (.github/actions/unit-tests/action.yml:27-63, .github/actions/dependency-audit/action.yml) or by root package scripts (package.json backfill:profile-pii)
the README's platform table documents only the local-stack/backup PowerShell+bash pairs; the one-off content scripts it does list (fix-*.js, generate-*) are exactly the ones with zero references
findings.impact: The index points maintainers at dead one-off scripts while hiding the guards that enforce schema/docs/RLS hygiene; a new contributor cannot discover the checks from the scripts entry point.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate the script index (or add a small script that diffs scripts/ against the README table, similar to check-required-checks.mjs) and move one-off entries into a 'historical' subsection.

findings.title: No circular-dependency guard; one live import cycle in the worker
evidence: Python import-graph scan of apps/api, apps/worker, apps/web (relative + @/ + @mct/* aliases), packages/sdk, packages/ui at 8d299b8d: 756 files with local imports, exactly 1 cycle

cycle: apps/worker/src/metrics.ts:2 imports getRegisteredTaskTypes from ./task-registry; apps/worker/src/task-registry.ts:3 imports taskExecutionsTotal/taskExecutionDuration from ./metrics (used at metrics.ts:105 inside getMetrics())
no dependency-cruiser / madge / eslint-plugin-import (import/no-cycle) anywhere in package.json files or .github/ workflows
cross-boundary direction is otherwise clean: 0 imports from one app into another, 0 imports from packages into apps (only type imports of @mct/sdk/database.types in api/worker)
findings.impact: The worker cycle is currently benign (both uses are inside functions), but nothing prevents the next one; cycles across modules are a classic source of undefined-at-import-time failures in the bundled worker/api builds.
findings.recommendation: Move the registry-length gauge read out of metrics.ts (pass the count in from the metrics endpoint caller) to break the cycle, and add madge --circular or eslint import/no-cycle as a non-blocking CI report, then make it blocking.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; cycle reproduced from source, not from a tool run (node/madge unavailable on the audit host).

findings.title: Explicit `any` is lint-disabled and 63 `supabase as any` casts sit at the typed-client boundary
evidence: packages/config/tsconfig.base.json:9 — "strict": true for all packages (good)

apps/api/eslint.config.js:21, apps/web/eslint.config.mjs:45, apps/worker/eslint.config.js:21 — "@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any": "off" in every app config; @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars is only "warn"

apps/api/src: 76 `: any`/`as any` occurrences outside tests, including 63 `supabase as any` (proposals.ts 13, approvals.ts 8, findings.ts 7, client-onboarding-command-center.ts 5, ...) — almost all at loadOwned(req, supabase as any, ...) call sites

apps/api/src/lib/tenant.ts:66-76 types loadOwned's client as a hand-written structural subset of SupabaseClient; apps/api/src/lib/db-types.ts provides sanctioned toJson/asInsert/asUpdate boundary helpers
0 @ts-ignore / @ts-expect-error in the repo; 15 eslint-disable lines, mostly @next/next/no-img-element with justification
findings.impact: The any-casts are localized but defeat the generated Database types exactly where tenant scoping is enforced (loadOwned); lint cannot flag new casts, so the pattern is spreading file by file.
findings.recommendation: Type loadOwned's client parameter as SupabaseClient<Database> (or a generic) and drop the casts; turn @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any back to "warn" so new occurrences are visible in review.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; counts are grep-based, no build/typecheck was run (node unavailable on the audit host).

findings.title: AGENTS.md (120 KB) doubles as a historical changelog and is mirrored into review.md
evidence: AGENTS.md — 1,003 lines / 120,423 bytes; the current-state contract is the top ~338 lines, then 'Audit findings ledger (2026-08-26)' at line 339, 'Prompt Pack Verification' at 425 and 'Completed Work' session logs from line 470 to EOF (sections dated 2026-08-26 through 2026-09-27)
review.md — 1,003 lines / 120,644 bytes, generated from AGENTS.md and guarded by scripts/sync-review-md.mjs --check (.github/actions/unit-tests/action.yml:63, validate.yml:110)
CHANGELOG.md exists and is maintained separately (468 lines, Unreleased section), so the session history in AGENTS.md is a second changelog
docs/audits/README.md:52-56 points readers at AGENTS.md 'Known Debt' and 'Completed Work' as the running audit summary
findings.impact: Every agent session and every review.md consumer loads ~240 KB of duplicated historical narrative; the current contract is buried, and two files must be kept in sync for every doc edit. The bloat also makes the doc-count guards fragile (they parse this file).
findings.recommendation: Move the ledger/completed-work sections to CHANGELOG.md or docs/audits history and keep AGENTS.md as a current-state contract (<300 lines); review.md then shrinks automatically.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; adjacent to HYG-P2-001 (corpus bloat) and DOC-P3-001 (dated audits) but a distinct file with its own fix.

findings.title: Audit run layout contract is not met by the committed repo-deep-dive runs
evidence: docs/audits/README.md layout contract requires docs/audits/<pack>/<run>/report.md per run ('report.md # human-readable findings + status')

docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261002-0344-develop-6286137/, 20261004-0700-main-178b91c/ and mainecybertech-20261004-full-main-9c0b88c/ contain no report.md (they ship INDEX.md / EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md / registers instead); the four manual runs do have report.md
docs/audits/README.md Runs table lists only the comprehensive and ui-ux runs; the three repo-deep-dive runs are absent from the index
docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/REAUDIT_REPORT_20261004.md sits at pack level rather than in a dated run directory, and its local references are machine paths (see HYG-P3-001)
findings.impact: The documented contract and the committed artifacts disagree, so tooling or agents that expect report.md (or the Runs index) cannot discover the audits; the pack-level re-audit report breaks the 'never overwrite / always a run dir' rule.
findings.recommendation: Either amend docs/audits/README.md to the actual layout (INDEX.md + registers) or rename the entry file to report.md; add the three runs to the Runs table and move/rename REAUDIT_REPORT_20261004.md into a run directory.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; artifact-layout hygiene, complementary to DOC-P3-001 (which is about staleness markers).

findings.title: Two Redis client libraries coexist in apps/api
evidence: apps/api/package.json — depends on both "redis": "^4.7.0" and "ioredis": "^5.11.1"
apps/api/src/lib/health.ts:1 and apps/api/src/middleware/cache.ts:2 import from "redis" (node-redis)
apps/api/src/lib/idempotency.ts:1 imports Redis from "ioredis"; the worker uses ioredis (BullMQ requirement)
pnpm-lock resolves one version of each (redis 4.7.1, ioredis 5.11.1) — no version duplication, but two client APIs and two connection pools
findings.impact: Two Redis clients mean duplicated connection/metrics handling and two upgrade paths for the same infrastructure dependency; operators must reason about both when tuning or rotating Redis credentials.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate on ioredis (already required by BullMQ) or document why node-redis is needed for health/cache; remove the other dependency.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; low urgency, both usages are real.

report:
# Repository Hygiene, Maintainability, and Code Health Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`
- Repository: `MaineCyberTech/mainecybertech` (`/tmp/opencode/mct-audit-target`, read-only)
- Branch: `main`
- Commit SHA: `8d299b8d`
- Generated at: 2026-10-11
- Auditor: domain subagent 21 (HYGIENE), full-pass rerun
- Area code: HYGIENE (previous register rows used `HYG`; verification rows keep their original titles)
- Output path: `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8/21_repo_hygiene_maintainability.md`
- Scope limitations: read-only static review; `node`, `pnpm` and `rg` are not installed on the audit host, so repo guards were re-implemented in short Python/`git grep` snippets and marked as such; no build, test, install or typecheck was run.

## Scope

Reviewed at `8d299b8d`: folder/file naming, duplicate/dead/unused code, generated and build artifacts, imports and circular dependencies, large files/components, type safety/`any`, error handling, TODO/FIXME, logging consistency, config sprawl, competing patterns, package scripts, dependency boundaries, test utilities, docs drift, changelog/ADRs. Not reviewed: runtime behaviour, database state, live GitHub settings, and anything requiring a build (typecheck/lint/test execution). Cross-domain rows (DOC, ACM, RLS, INV, AI) were not duplicated; where a previous row is owned by another area it was left to that owner (see Open Questions).

## Evidence Reviewed

| Evidence | Type | Why relevant | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `git ls-files`, `git ls-files -s`, `git ls-files --eol`, `du -cb` | inventory | file set, exec bits, EOLs, corpus size | 2,823 tracked files; 19 `.sh` all 100755; 0 CRLF files |
| `prompts/manifest.json` + `scripts/verify-prompts.js` algorithm | generated artifact | pinning guard | Python replica (utf8 + CRLF-normalise SHA-256): 630/630 match, 0 mismatches |
| `apps/api/src/data/products.json` vs `apps/web/lib/catalog/data/products.json` (+2 pack copies) | data | duplicate catalogs | 245 common SKUs, 245 differ in 6 fields; 3 distinct copies |
| Import-graph scan (Python, relative + `@/` + `@mct/*`) | code | circular deps / boundaries | 756 files with local imports; 1 cycle; 0 cross-app imports |
| Orphan scan (exact symbol grep) over `apps/**`, `packages/**` | code | dead code | 3 dead lib modules, 1 dead component, 7 dead scripts, 1 dead duplicate snippet |
| `apps/web/components/admin/AdminDocumentsCenterClient.tsx` | code | large component | 2,322 lines, one component, 26 state/effect hooks |
| ESLint/TS configs (`apps/*/eslint.config.*`, `packages/config/tsconfig.base.json`) | config | type safety, unused vars | `strict: true`; `no-explicit-any` off; `no-unused-vars` warn |
| `.gitignore`, `.github/actions/dependency-audit/action.yml`, `validate.yml` | CI/config | generated artifacts + exec-bit guard | licenses/SBOM untracked and gated; exec-bit gate present |
| `scripts/README.md` vs `scripts/` listing | docs | docs drift | 14 scripts (10 active guards) undocumented; "Last updated 2026-08-01" |
| `docs/audits/README.md` + run directories | docs/artifacts | artifact layout contract | 3 repo-deep-dive runs lack `report.md`; Runs table omits them |
| `AGENTS.md` / `review.md` / `CHANGELOG.md` / `docs/adr/README.md` | docs | agent contract, changelog/ADRs | AGENTS.md 1,003 lines/120 KB; review.md generated mirror; 11 ADRs (7 table-only, disclosed) |
| Markdown link check (Python replica of `check-docs-links.mjs`, extended to all 294 non-audit md) | docs | docs drift | 0 broken links |
| Previous run `follow_up_register.md` HYG rows + `PORT-P2-001` | register | verification duty | re-verified at 8d299b8d (table below) |

## Verification Performed

| Command / check | Observed result |
|---|---|
| `git ls-files -s '*.sh' \| awk '{print $1}' \| sort \| uniq -c` | `19 100755`, 0 files at 100644 → PORT-P2-001 fixed |
| `sed -n '19,31p' .github/workflows/validate.yml` | exec-bit guard present (PORT-001), fails the deploy gate on any 100644 `.sh` |
| Python replica of `scripts/verify-prompts.js` verify | 630/630 manifest hashes match at 8d299b8d; 0 missing/added/changed |
| Python structural diff of the four `products.json` copies | API vs web: 245/245 differ (6 fields each); pack data vs pack repo_patch: byte-identical; both differ from the apps |
| `git grep -nE '\bgenerateProposal\b' \| grep -v proposal-actions.ts` | 0 hits → dead stub confirmed |

## Executive Summary

The repo's *guards* are unusually good: exec bits, prompt provenance, docs links/counts, generated DB types, OpenAPI coverage, review.md mirror and SBOM/license tracking are all machine-checked in CI, and every one of those checks reproduces clean at `8d299b8d`. Docs links: 0 broken across 294 markdown files. Dependency boundaries are clean (no cross-app imports, single lockfile versions). TODO/FIXME debt is essentially zero in source (1 ops note).

The *debt* is concentrated in three places. First, duplication: the product catalog exists in four files with three different contents, and the API copy is a stale generation of the web copy. Second, orphans: three dead lib modules, one dead component, seven unreferenced one-off scripts plus their 1.2 MB content-map pipeline, and a stray duplicate seed snippet. Third, generated artifacts that escaped the otherwise-good gates: seven committed `.pyc` files and a stale `apps/web/public/version.json`. One 2,322-line component is the main complexity hotspot; one benign import cycle exists in the worker with no cycle-detection tooling.

Recommended next actions: delete the dead modules/scripts/component and the stray snippet (single cleanup PR), reconcile the catalog copies behind one canonical source, add `__pycache__`/`version.json` handling, fix the known-broken `sbom:licenses` script, and split `AdminDocumentsCenterClient.tsx`.
